rationale: The claim asserts NP-hardness of SETsparse via a deterministic polynomial-time many-one reduction from 3-SAT. The reduction-completeness meta-principle directly supports this reasoning: an efficient answer-preserving reduction from a known NP-complete problem transfers hardness to the target problem. The reduction type, worst-case complexity scale, and problem-instance variables are compatible.
